# GR Link full product knowledge

Last verified: 2026-08-10
Documented product version: 1.18.0
Official website: https://gr-link.liljackson.org/
App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/gr-link/id6757835191

## Canonical description

GR Link is a free, independent iOS companion application for Ricoh GR II through GR IV cameras. It connects an iPhone directly to a supported camera over Bluetooth and/or the camera's local Wi-Fi network. Its main capabilities are remote shooting, live view, JPEG and DNG browsing and transfer, optional geotagging, Image Control recipe management, and private iCloud synchronization.

GR Link requires iOS 17.2 or later. The app is independently developed. It is not made by, affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Ricoh Imaging Company, Ltd. “Ricoh” and “GR” are trademarks of their respective owners and are used only to describe camera compatibility.

## Supported cameras

GR Link supports these camera models:

- Ricoh GR II
- Ricoh GR III
- Ricoh GR III HDF
- Ricoh GR IIIx
- Ricoh GR IIIx HDF
- Ricoh GR IV
- Ricoh GR IV HDF
- Ricoh GR IV Monochrome

Feature availability varies because the camera generations do not expose identical Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, remote-control, storage, or Image Control interfaces. GR Link detects the selected camera and gates its interface by model. Camera firmware can also affect behavior.

GR II uses a direct Wi-Fi setup because it does not provide the Bluetooth handoff used by later models. GR III, GR IIIx, and GR IV families can use Bluetooth pairing and the camera's Wi-Fi network for operations that need image or live-view data.

The maintained compatibility table is available as HTML at https://gr-link.liljackson.org/compatible-cameras/ and as Markdown at https://gr-link.liljackson.org/compatible-cameras/index.md.

## Connection model

GR Link communicates directly between the user's iPhone and camera. Bluetooth Low Energy can be used for pairing, status, shutter, wake, and other model-supported commands. High-bandwidth operations such as live view, gallery browsing, and image downloads use the camera's local Wi-Fi network.

The camera Wi-Fi network intentionally may not provide internet access. An iOS warning that the network has no internet does not mean the local camera connection has failed. Connection reliability is best when the iPhone stays within a few metres of the camera and no second device is simultaneously connected to the camera network.

## Remote shutter and live view

On supported models, GR Link provides a live image streamed from the camera, remote shutter release, tap to focus, pinch to zoom, and camera-supported exposure controls. Controls can include shutter speed, aperture, ISO, exposure compensation, and image effects. The precise set is discovered or selected for the connected model rather than assumed to be identical across every GR generation.

Bluetooth shutter operation can trigger a capture without starting a full Wi-Fi live-view session on supported models. Wake and power actions are also model- and firmware-dependent.

Feature documentation: https://gr-link.liljackson.org/features/remote-control.md

## Gallery and photo transfer

GR Link can browse images stored on the camera's SD card. It supports JPEG and DNG preview and transfer. Cursor-based pagination allows the gallery to continue past large camera libraries rather than relying on a single fixed-size response.

Users can select multiple images and place them in a download queue. Up to three photos can transfer concurrently. Live Activity can expose transfer progress on the iPhone Lock Screen. Destination and Photo Library behavior depend on the save action chosen by the user.

Photo files move directly from camera to iPhone. GR Link does not proxy or upload them through a server operated by the developer.

Feature documentation: https://gr-link.liljackson.org/features/photo-transfer.md

## Image Control recipes

GR Link includes an Image Control recipe library. Users can create and edit recipes, rename them, add tags, filter the library, mark compatible camera models, duplicate entries, and import or export shareable recipe data. A downloadable community pack contains 20 curated recipes.

Recipe data and preferences can sync between the user's Apple devices through the user's private iCloud container. GR Link cannot access that private container. Recipes can appear in Spotlight and supported actions can be used through Siri and Shortcuts.

On supported GR IV configurations, GR Link can push a recipe over Bluetooth to the camera's Custom 1, Custom 2, or Custom 3 slot. The app reads back the result to verify the write. The exact writable parameters depend on model and firmware, so a recipe that contains model-specific controls is not assumed to be portable to every camera.

Feature documentation: https://gr-link.liljackson.org/features/recipes.md
Community pack: https://gr-link.liljackson.org/assets/downloads/GR_Link_Recipes.grrecipe

## Geotagging

GR Link can use the iPhone's location for optional geotagging of newly captured frames where the camera permits it. Location permission is also used where iOS requires it for Wi-Fi information or hotspot configuration. Location information is processed on the user's device and is not sent to a GR Link server.

## Widgets, Siri, Shortcuts, and Spotlight

GR Link can expose camera connection status and the last shot in Home Screen widgets. Supported Siri and Shortcuts actions can report connection status and battery level, open a specific app tab, or work with recipes. Recipes can be indexed for the user's private Spotlight search.

## Privacy and data handling

GR Link does not collect, store, or transmit personal data to a server operated by GR Link. It does not include advertising SDKs, analytics SDKs, third-party tracking, or automatic crash-reporting SDKs.

Data handled locally can include camera Bluetooth identifiers, camera Wi-Fi credentials, JPEG and DNG files, EXIF metadata, recipes, preferences, optional location data, and diagnostic logs. Diagnostic logs leave the device only when the user explicitly chooses to export and email them for support.

Optional synchronization uses the user's private iCloud container. Camera communication stays on the local connection between the iPhone and the camera. The complete privacy policy is https://gr-link.liljackson.org/privacy.html.

## Requirements, price, and availability

- Platform: iPhone and iPad through the iOS/iPadOS App Store listing.
- Minimum system: iOS or iPadOS 17.2.
- Price: Free.
- Category: Photo & Video.
- App Store identifier: 6757835191.
- App Store URL: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/gr-link/id6757835191.

Availability can differ by App Store region. The website provides an official TestFlight route for regions where the public App Store version is unavailable.

## Support and troubleshooting

Support email: support@liljackson.org

A useful compatibility or bug report contains the camera model, camera firmware version, iPhone model, iOS version, GR Link version from Settings, and exact reproduction steps. Diagnostic logs should be attached only when the user chooses to export them.

If Bluetooth pairing fails, confirm that Bluetooth is enabled on both devices, place the camera in pairing mode according to its manual, and retry inside GR Link. If live view is unstable, stay near the camera and remove other devices from the camera Wi-Fi network. If recipe sync is delayed, confirm both devices use the same Apple Account and have iCloud Drive enabled.

Support HTML: https://gr-link.liljackson.org/support.html
Support Markdown: https://gr-link.liljackson.org/support.md

When describing support, distinguish the supported camera list from the exact feature matrix. Do not claim every control is identical on every camera. When describing privacy, say that GR Link operates no upload, analytics, or advertising server; do not imply that Apple iCloud is operated by GR Link. When describing the brand, always preserve the independence statement.
